criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear mission purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), explicit users (marine/conservation scientists), strong need justification with statistics and four cited literature sources. Slightly light on formal requirements/objectives, but well within Accomplished.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed Gantt chart with week-by-week tasks, deadlines and narrative tying each task to the mission (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, end of life). However, no explicit contingency provision for project variations, keeping it at the lower Accomplished bound.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.
The goal is to brainstorm and research as many possible strategies for the satellite’s launch/orbit and then gradually cut and refine them

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress is mostly background reading and STK tutorial completion; no preliminary technical results (no orbit, coverage, or link calculations) are presented or interpreted. On track, but work shown is minor rather than a good preliminary result set.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure, well-written, consistent formatting, labelled Gantt figure with legend explained in text. Footnoted URLs match in-text citations. Minor issues: 'Useful Links' section is uncited in text and bare URLs rather than formatted references; report is short of typical depth.

evidence.quote: Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution leading to the bleaching of coral reefs.¹

technical_issues.issue: Claims near-real-time relay without discussing orbit/coverage implications (e.g. LEO revisit gaps vs GEO); feasibility not yet addressed.
No contingency/slack provision in the Gantt chart for project variations.
Preliminary progress lacks any quantitative technical work (no orbit parameters, coverage, or link budget estimates).

overall: Strong mission concept and rationale for an Australian reef-monitoring satellite with good referencing and a detailed Gantt-chart plan. Preliminary technical progress is limited to tutorials and reading, and the plan lacks contingencies; presentation is clean and professional.

feedback.summary: A strong preliminary report: your Great Barrier Reef monitoring concept is well justified with cited literature, and your week-by-week Gantt chart is detailed and mission-linked. Presentation is clean and professional. To lift your mark, add contingency planning to your schedule and, most importantly, show quantitative technical progress — orbit, coverage or link-budget estimates — rather than tutorials and reading alone.
next_steps: Add contingency/slack provision to your Gantt chart (e.g. buffer weeks or alternate task paths) and explain how you would handle project variations.
Produce at least one preliminary technical result: candidate orbit parameters, revisit/coverage analysis, or a first-order link budget, with brief interpretation.
Address the feasibility of near-real-time relay: compare LEO revisit gaps vs GEO coverage for your users' needs.
Convert the 'Useful Links' section into properly formatted, in-text-cited references consistent with your footnoting style.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly states the purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), identifies users (marine and conservation scientists), and justifies need with statistics and four cited sources. Next level: strengthen formal mission goals, objectives and requirements, and discuss orbit/coverage implications of your near-real-time relay claim (LEO revisit gaps vs GEO).
criteria.C2: Accomplished (7/10). Your Gantt chart with weekly tasks and deadlines is detailed and each task is tied to the mission narrative (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, end of life). To move higher, add explicit contingency provision for project variations — buffer time or fallback strategies — and show applied course material (orbits, coverage) in the plan.
criteria.C3: Adequate (5/10). Your progress so far is background reading (Asner's Hawaii system, coral bleaching) and STK tutorials 1–4, which shows you are on track but is minor work. The next level requires a good preliminary set of results with description and interpretation — e.g. orbit parameters, coverage analysis, or link budget estimates from STK.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (7/10). Your report has a clear logical structure, consistent formatting, well-written prose, and a labelled Gantt figure with the legend explained in text; footnoted citations match sources. To improve further: cite the 'Useful Links' section in text and format those bare URLs as proper references, and deepen the technical content.
